answers: N, c, r, r, H, W

hints: Output position (h*r + i, w*r + j) means the height index is h major and i minor.
After unfolding the axes are (N, c, i, j, h, w); you want (N, c, h, i, w, j) before merging pairs.

title: U-Net double convolution
description: One U-Net level: (3x3 conv -> BatchNorm -> ReLU) applied twice. Convolutions only get a bias when there is no BatchNorm after them (BN's shift makes it redundant).
code:
class DoubleConv(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, padding=1, batch_norm=True):
        super().__init__()
        use_bias = batch_norm
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size=3, stride=1, padding=padding, bias=use_bias)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size=3, stride=1, padding=padding, bias=use_bias)
        self.bn1 = nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels) if batch_norm else nn.Identity()
        self.bn2 = nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels) if batch_norm else nn.Identity()

    def forward(self, x):
        x = F.relu(self.bn1(self.conv1(x)))
        x = F.relu(self.conv2(self.bn2(x)))
        return x

errors.explanation: Bias is only needed without BatchNorm; with BN it is redundant, so it should be `not batch_norm`.

fixes: self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(out_channels, out_channels, kernel_size=3, stride=1, padding=padding, bias=use_bias)
self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(out_channels, out_channels, kernel_size=3, padding=padding, bias=use_bias)
self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(out_channels, out_channels, 3, stride=1, padding=padding, bias=use_bias)
errors.explanation: The second convolution consumes the first one's output, so its input has out_channels channels.
The order is conv -> BN -> ReLU; here bn2 is applied before conv2.

hints: Look at the bias flag, the channel arguments of conv2, and the layer order in forward.
Is `use_bias` true or false when batch_norm is True?
use_bias = not batch_norm; conv2 takes out_channels; relu(bn2(conv2(x))).

title: ResNet-18 encoder with U-Net decoder
description: Runs the pretrained ResNet-18 stages while remembering the feature map at each resolution, then decodes with skips from deepest to shallowest, restores the full resolution and predicts per-pixel class logits.

def forward(self, x):
    s0 = self.stem(x)                       # 64  @ H/2
    s1 = self.layer1(s0)
    s2 = self.layer2(s1)                    # 128 @ H/8
    s3 = self.layer3(s2)                    # 256 @ H/16
    x = self.layer4(s3)                     # 512 @ H/32
    x = self.decoder[0](x, s3)
    x = self.decoder[1](x, s2)
    x = self.decoder[2](x, s1)
    x = self.decoder[3](x, s3)
    x = self.final_up(x)
    return self.head(x)
